title: Extract facet-to-field mapping as reusable guard extension point
context: nuryel_write is a fourth auto-committing tool with identical worktree-misroute exposure as the three already-guarded tools, but was left uncovered. Adding a guard per tool risks duplication and divergence; the guard logic itself is already shared. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Extract the facet-to-file-evidence-field mapping into a `fileEvidenceFor` helper function, allowing the existing `misrouteGuard` to work for any tool that names files, rather than embedding field-name knowledge in each tool's handler.
consequences: nuryel_write's decisions/findings/bugs facets are now protected from committing to the wrong worktree when cwd is omitted
The facet-to-field-name mapping is centralized and explicit, making coverage boundaries visible and preventing silent gaps
Future auto-committing tools can reuse the same guard pattern without duplication
bugs facet is protected even though the three older tools never wrote it (consistent coverage)
alternatives_rejected: Duplicate misrouteGuard logic in nuryel_write's handler (code duplication, divergence risk)
Create a separate guard function specific to nuryel_write (unnecessary proliferation)
Leave nuryel_write unguarded but document it separately (silently defers the hazard)
